howDoI.q: How do I make a room play a song?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Sounds and Music is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels about songs and sound effects, and takes a few minutes to finish. Turn your sound up.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: A Song Per Room
pages.html:
Level 1: A Song Per Room

This room has a song, and it starts the moment the room loads. The EACH ROOM HAS ITS OWN SONG sign comes first, then A SONG REPEATS UNTIL YOU LEAVE: wait a little and you will hear it start over. Four coins are on the way. The THE NEXT ROOM PLAYS A NEW SONG sign stands by the exit, because it does.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The song is a file. meadow.cmf is a Sound Blaster song. You can open it in the music editor and play it there.
  • The scene names it. Open sounds.gam in the scenes editor and pick the first level’s scene. One of its file slots is Sound Blaster music, and it holds meadow.cmf. The room plays that file whenever the scene loads.
  • It repeats. When the song reaches its end the engine starts it again, so a room needs no loop of its own.
  • The title and menu are scenes too, each with its own music slot. This game gives them the same song.
  • The coins are 10 points each, and each plays the score sound. Level 2 says more about that.

pages.head: Level 2: Sounds on Pickups
pages.html:
Level 2: Sounds on Pickups

A new room, and a new song, a waltz. The signs name four sounds in turn: COINS PLAY THE SCORE SOUND (three coins), A BAG PLAYS THE MONEY SOUND (two bags), A SPIKE PLAYS THE HURT SOUND (one spike, which takes 10 of Nova’s 30 hit points, once) and A HEART PLAYS THE HELP SOUND (two hearts, which give the 20 back). Listen: they are all different beeps.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A different song. The second level’s scene names waltz.cmf in its music slot, and the first named meadow.cmf. Going through the door loads the new scene, so the old song stops and the new one starts from its first note.
  • One sound a counter. Game-Maker plays a sound by itself when a counter changes: score up plays Add score, money up plays Add money, hit points up plays Help, a life up plays Add life. They are the first nine entries in sounds.snd, in the sound editor.
  • The bag. Open sounds.bbl in the blocks editor and pick bag. Its Touch tab says Effect counter 3 (money) and Amount 1. Money is a counter like hit points, so Nova needs a starting number for it in hero.chr.
  • The coin is the Starter blocks’ own: Score points 10 and nothing else.
  • The hurt. The spike takes 10 hit points, and the engine plays the sound written on the hero’s Hurt sequence in hero.chr. That is sound 10 here.
  • Changing one. Open sounds.snd and change the PC speaker notes of one entry. Play the level again and that pickup has a new beep.

pages.head: Level 3: A Quiet Room
pages.html:
Level 3: A Quiet Room

No song plays here, which makes the sounds easy to hear. The THIS ROOM HAS NO SONG sign comes first. Then JUMPING HAS A SOUND TOO: press Space and Nova’s jump beeps. Hop up onto the ledge for its three coins. Near the end the A NEW SOUND CUTS OFF THE LAST ONE sign stands before a row of five coins. Run through them and hear each beep cut short by the next.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • No song. This level’s scene leaves the Sound Blaster music slot empty. When a scene loads, the engine stops the old song first and then plays whatever the slot holds, so an empty slot is silence.
  • A sound on a move. Open hero.chr in the character editor and pick the Jump sequence. Its Sound is 9. Any of Nova’s sequences can name any of the 30 sounds in sounds.snd, and it plays each time the sequence starts.
  • One at a time. The engine has one sound voice. A new sound replaces the one still playing, so five coins in a row play only the start of each beep.
  • The ledge is planks, solid on top only, so Nova jumps up through them and stands on top.

pages.head: What it can and can't do
pages.html:
What the engine can and can't do

  • A song belongs to a scene. It starts when the scene loads and repeats. There is no block, monster or key that starts or stops a song in the middle of a room. To change the music, link to another scene.
  • A song starts over whenever its scene loads again, even if the same file plays next door.
  • Songs need a Sound Blaster. Without one the room is silent. Only the sound effects have a PC speaker version.
  • A sound set has 30 sounds. The first nine are played by counters changing (score, money, a life, hit points and a monster squashed). Each of the other 21 is played only when a character sequence names it.
  • A block can’t play a sound by itself. It plays one by changing a counter or hit points. A block that must make a noise gets a counter, or the hero a sequence.
  • One sound at a time, and no volume or pan for either songs or sounds.
  • Recorded sounds. Each entry can also name a recorded .voc file for the Sound Blaster to play in place of the beep. This game uses only beeps.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Give level 3 a song: put meadow.cmf in its scene’s music slot.
  • Swap the songs of levels 1 and 2.
  • Open waltz.cmf in the music editor and change a few notes.
  • Give the Hurt sequence the sound the coin uses, and hear spikes sound friendly.
  • Make the bag give 5 money instead of 1.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a gold beanie crosses three short rooms: one with a bouncy song, one with a waltz, one that is quiet. Coins, money bags, hearts and spikes each beep differently, and jumping has a beep too. Read the signs, listen, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a song.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A room names its own song; leave it blank and the room is quiet
Every pickup and hurt has a sound you can change
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Three short levels about what a game sounds like. A room names its own song, and the next room can play a different one, or none. Coins, bags, hearts and spikes each play a sound of their own, and jumping has one too. Signs say how. Play it with the sound up, then open it in Game-Maker and change a song or a beep.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.
